name: Glandularia

project_scope.note: The accepted autonym Glandularia bipinnatifida var. bipinnatifida is taught inside canonical G. bipinnatifida rather than duplicated.

priority: mature LEAF dissection (featherlike secondary lobes vs fan-shaped primary lobes)
fruiting spike elongation (strong in bipinnatifida vs weak in pumila)
flower head/leaf attachment vs Verbena genus
study_strategy.warning: Do not confuse the Glandularia bipinnatifida var. bipinnatifida autonym with a third species. Do not split Glandularia from Verbena based only on color or leaf lobing: both genera can have lobed leaves and clustered flowers.

quick_split: G. bipinnatifida — larger/coarser plant with strongly and often twice-pinnately dissected, feathery leaves.
G. pumila — lower, compact plant with smaller broad leaves cut into fewer broader lobes and a short dense spike.
comparison_lesson.caveat: Older regional treatments may show G. bipinnatifida var. bipinnatifida; this project does not count that autonym as a second canonical species.

curation_status.genus_audit: prior science preserved, visual gap explicit
curation_status.visual_status: local public-source real photos cover both species; actual fruit macro comparisons missing

look_here_first: Glandularia: low spreading vervain relatives with OPPOSITE deeply lobed leaves and rounded, crowded flower clusters on short terminal spikes. For these two local species, start with one mature leaf: FEATHERY twice-cut = often G. bipinnatifida; small BROAD fan-lobed = often G. pumila. Then verify whether the old fruiting spike grows longer.
diagnostic_photo_checklist: matched mature flowering and fruiting spikes

species_comparison_matrix.bipinnatifida: Large, fernlike, 1–2-pinnately divided with numerous narrow ultimate segments
species_comparison_matrix.pumila: Small, broad ovate/triangular outline; 3–6 paired wider fan-like primary lobes and sublobes

species_comparison_matrix.bipinnatifida: Dense, frequently flat-to-rounded top; corolla limb ca. 8–12 mm wide (UT Williamson)
species_comparison_matrix.pumila: Small densely clustered pink/purple flowers; corolla limb ca. 7–8 mm across

species_comparison_matrix.bipinnatifida: Rachis often lengthens; persistent flowers/calyces separate visibly
species_comparison_matrix.pumila: Rachis scarcely lengthens; head remains compact

species_comparison_matrix.bipinnatifida: Usually more spreading/coarse; 10–40 cm tall in Williamson study
species_comparison_matrix.pumila: Often low delicate annual; up to ~19 cm in Williamson study

species_comparison_matrix.bipinnatifida: Longer calyx ~6.5–8 mm; bract about equaling or slightly exceeding calyx (UT Williamson)
species_comparison_matrix.pumila: Shorter calyx ~6–6.5 mm; bract slightly shorter than calyx ~5–6 mm; stalked glands

overlap_cautions: Flower color and height overlap; inspect mature leaves and fruiting spikes.
Existing G. bipinnatifida autonym is represented in its parent canonical card, not a separate species.
review_handoff: Confirm calyx/bract dimensions and indumentum as quantitative separators before adding numeric key thresholds.
shared_genus_traits: Herbaceous annuals/short-lived perennials in the local two-species set; low spreading, sometimes rooting at nodes.
Opposite/decussate simple leaves that are usually incised or divided into lobes; never confuse deeply lobed leaves with compound leaves.
Often hairy 4-sided stems and glandular calyx/bract structures.
Dense terminal spikes often look like round flower heads in full bloom; individual flowers have a slender corolla tube and usually five short spreading lobes.
Flowers form four dry single-seeded nutlets (mericarps); persistence and elongation of fruiting axis is a useful species character.
lookalikes: Verbena spp.: inspect leaves, mature spikes, and calyx.
G. bipinnatifida var. bipinnatifida: already included within parent species.

quick_key.if: Mature leaves comparatively large, feathery, once to TWICE pinnately cut with many narrow segment tips; fruiting spike elongates and becomes spaced
Mature leaves usually small, broadly ovate/triangular with 3–6 pairs of wide, fan-like primary lobes; fruiting spike stays SHORT and compact

comparison_cards.title: Prairie verbena vs low verbena — compare the leaf FIRST
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Take a photo of one mature leaf on each plant, then look for SECONDARY cuts. Prairie verbena is finely dissected and feathery; low verbena is smaller, with broad fan-like lobes. Then compare old fruiting spikes: elongated versus still short.

field_matrix.bipinnatifida: Deeply 1–2-pinnately cut into slender ultimate segments
field_matrix.pumila: Small broad blade with 3–6 paired fan-shaped major lobes and sublobes

comparison_cards.caution: Both plants have locally stored source-licensed species photos, but old fruiting spikes remain missing; do not infer mature spike elongation from photographs of flower buds.

comparison_cards.title: Prairie verbena or a true Verbena?
comparison_cards.look_here_first: A short, crowded head at flower time plus highly divided leaves suggests these local Glandularia species. More elongated, often sparse spikes and broader variation in leaf/hair architecture suggest Verbena. BUT Glandularia fruiting spikes lengthen and certain Verbena have compact tips; check species traits, not just genus silhouette.

field_matrix.glandularia: Usually dense rounded terminal spike in local examples
field_matrix.verbena: Frequently elongated flowering spikes with flowers spaced along an axis; exception: some compact-spiked species

field_matrix.glandularia: Often noticeably cut and lobed; our two local cards sharply differ in lobe width
field_matrix.verbena: Range from deeply divided (V. halei) to 3-lobed (V. xutha) to simple coarse (V. scabra)

field_matrix.glandularia: G. bipinnatifida's fernlike leaves and tight heads can resemble V. halei at first glance
field_matrix.verbena: V. halei has often open slender spikes and upper narrow/simple leaves

field_matrix.glandularia: Four nutlets; G. bipinnatifida's spike often elongates in fruit
field_matrix.verbena: Four nutlets as well; NOT a stand-alone genus key

comparison_cards.caution: This is an educational initial split, not a formal all-species determination key. Common names 'prairie verbena' and 'vervain' do not establish genus.

visual_comparison.subtitle: Both exact species now have licensed locally stored real botanical photos; compare mature leaf lobes, but actual same-scale old fruiting spike comparison is still needed.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: FEATHERY leaf + elongating fruit spike → G. bipinnatifida. Small FAN-shaped leaf + compact old fruit spike → G. pumila.
